evidence.note: decision 94 (her call of 2026-10-28: 'Sweden's rules'): the first year out of work on the person's own net money wage at exit, fixed for the spell (the a-kassa); after it a floor indexed to prices (social assistance: the riksnorm plus reasonable housing). The layer pays support on net0 (the aggregate net wage bill) times the share out of work, so a share acts on the MEAN net wage; the floor is flat, so its bill does not depend on whom it replaces

a_kassa.law: Lag (2024:506) om arbetslöshetsförsäkring (decisions from 1 Oct 2025): 5 kap. 2 § and 3 kap. 12 § — the base is 1/12 of earned income in the 12 months before the claim month (the person's own money wage at exit), set once for the benefit period; 5 kap. 4-6 §§ — 80% for a member of at least 12 months (60% for 6-11, 50% otherwise); 5 kap. 10 § — down 10 pp after 100 benefit days and 5 pp more after 200; 4 kap. 4 § — at most 300 days. https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/lag-2024506-om-arbetsloshetsforsakring_sfs-2024-506/
a_kassa.ceiling: Förordning (2024:1350) om arbetslöshetsförsäkring 7 §: the highest income base 34,000 SEK (a month: IAF, 'Högsta ersättningsgrundande inkomst är 34 000 kronor i månaden'), a fixed sum. https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/forordning-20241350-om-arbetsloshetsforsakring_sfs-2024-1350/ ; https://www.iaf.se/lag-ratt/ny-arbetsloshetsforsakring-fran-1-oktober/

riksnorm_2026.source: Regeringen, 'Riksnorm för 2026 fastställd' (13 Nov 2025): every item +0.7% on 2025, set on Konsumentverket's price and consumption surveys; housing, electricity, work travel, home insurance and union / a-kassa fees are paid separately at reasonable cost. https://www.regeringen.se/artiklar/2025/11/riksnorm-for-2026-faststalld/ ; https://www.socialstyrelsen.se/kunskapsstod-och-regler/omraden/ekonomiskt-bistand/riksnormen/

rent_2026.source: SCB, Hyror i bostadslägenheter 2026 (2 Oct 2026), nationwide means. https://www.scb.se/hitta-statistik/statistik-efter-amne/boende-bebyggelse-och-mark/bostader-och-boende/hyror-i-bostadslagenheter/pong/statistiknyhet/hyror-i-bostadslagenheter-2026

wages_2025.source: SCB, Lönespridning efter sektor och kön 2025, whole economy. https://www.scb.se/hitta-statistik/statistik-efter-amne/arbetsmarknad/loner-och-arbetskostnader/lonestrukturstatistik-hela-ekonomin/pong/tabell-och-diagram/lonespridning-efter-sektor-och-kon-2024/

employment_ths.source: Eurostat lfsq_egaps (SE, total, 15-74, EMP / SAL, thousand persons; updated 2026-09-11), the mean of 2025Q3-2026Q2 (the quarters of sweden_start's wage bill), read 28 Oct 2026

sensitivity.0.27: a cohabiting couple's per-person norm sharing a two-room flat: 0.2706
sensitivity.0.43: a single adult in a two-room flat: 0.4316

floor_share.note: fixed from this evidence, not tuned on results; the median earner's 0.41 would overstate the flat floor's aggregate bill

replacement_first.note: 0.65 kept (her call set the base, not the rate); the a-kassa's aggregate gross rate under today's 34,000 SEK ceiling is about 0.51 (net a few points lower: benefits get no earned-income tax credit), so 0.65 overstates the start's first-year bill by about a quarter; the fixed ceiling binds less as money wages fall (the effective rate rises toward 0.73). The ceiling is not modelled; the sensitivity runs 0.51

caveats: social assistance is means-tested by household (a partner's income, assets); the layer pays the floor to everyone out of work after the first year
aktivitetsstöd (activity support within programmes) is ignored
the first year is 4 quarters against the a-kassa's 300 days (about 60 weeks)
electricity and insurance are left out of the floor
the a-kassa's nominal ceiling is not modelled

the support bill is reported, not financed: support_cost_pct_gdp feeds neither the macro block's deficit nor the layer's 0.30 tax (the macro block's own fiscal bridge pays dependants 0.30 of a support basket in real terms)

calibration.source: results/calibration_c.json calibrations['c_central_lo']['targets'], re-solved by macro.calibrate_c; equal to the stored params bit for bit

alternative: benefits follow the current.note: benefit_base='wage': public support is the replacement rate (0.65 in the first year, 0.50 after) on the current net money wage, so benefits follow wages — the named alternative to Sweden's rules (decision 94), the default of 27-28 Oct 2026. The family-based variants are left out: they run on this rule already.

sensitivity: the floor's level.note: Sweden's rules with the floor at 0.27 (a cohabiting couple's per-person riksnorm sharing a two-room flat) and 0.43 (a single adult in a two-room flat) of the start's mean net wage, against the central 0.36 (a single adult in a one-room flat). Not the default.

sensitivity: the first year at the aggre.note: Sweden's rules with the first year at 0.51, the a-kassa's aggregate gross rate under today's 34,000 SEK ceiling, against the layer's 0.65. Not the default.

sensitivity: the family-based regime on.note: the family-based regime on Sweden's structure — its first year (0.40) on the money wage at exit, then a price-indexed floor at its own later rate (0.25) — in place of its pinned rule (benefits follow the current money wage): the open question for her under decision 94. Not the default.

sensitivity: benefits on the wage at exi.note: benefit_base='exit': public support on each cohort's real net wage when it left work, indexed to prices after; the layer's rule (Sweden's, decision 94) pays the first year on the money wage at exit and then a price-indexed floor. Not the default.

sensitivity: benefits on the start's rea.note: benefit_base='start': public support on the start's real net wage, indexed to prices — the rule before the refit, whose benefits exceed the wage lost once money wages fall far enough. Not the default.

sensitivity: rigid wages, no money-wage.note: wage_fall_max=0: money wages never fall (the rigidity before the refit), with the refit's job loss (log employment falls by the labour-demand elasticity times the log excess). Not the default.
